mbm-0218.clue: I save the last dot for my sister.
mbm-0218.quote: We wore the left button smooth playing a maze game after school. On her birthday I cleared the whole screen except one bright dot and left the controller on her dinner plate.

mbm-0219.clue: That speck on the biscuit tin is moving.
mbm-0219.quote: I keep my binoculars in the kitchen. One cold morning I watched a tiny wren peck crumbs out of the hinge of the biscuit tin on the step. It found breakfast where even I couldn’t.

mbm-0220.clue: I drew a wire between the two mugs.
mbm-0220.quote: My radio friend collects mugs. We described our favorites to each other, then mailed drawings. Her sketch of my chipped whale mug is so good I use it as a coaster for the original.

mbm-0221.clue: There’s a silver thread in the haystack.
mbm-0221.quote: From under the parachute I saw a silver path through a field. Back on the ground it turned out to be a little stream with a kingfisher. I’d driven past it for years.

mbm-0222.clue: We bowl from the crooked shell.
mbm-0222.quote: Our wicket on the beach kept sliding in the sand, so we made it from three pieces of driftwood tied like a tripod. The first good hit rang them together like wind chimes.

mbm-0223.quote: My uncle can’t grip a slippery handle. I pressed his thumb into soft clay and built a handle around the dent. The first time he poured tea he didn’t spill a drop.

mbm-0224.clue: I carry a pencil that floats.
mbm-0224.quote: I draw the things I can see only from my kayak. A little blue house under the jetty turned out to be bait boxes stacked on top of each other. It still looks like a palace in my sketch.

mbm-0225.clue: I putt with a red pencil behind my ear.
mbm-0225.quote: I’ve drawn the lighthouse on hole nine every year since I was ten. Last month they repainted it yellow. I had to buy a whole new pencil for the occasion.

mbm-0226.clue: The stone in my pocket has a flat bottom.
mbm-0226.quote: It came from a trail where we stopped to make coffee. My cup kept tipping until I set it on that stone. At home it holds my spoon and always reminds me where the view was.

mbm-0227.clue: We use a map that can get rained on.
mbm-0227.quote: Our board-game island is painted on an oilcloth. When my cousin upset his juice, we declared a flood and moved the villages uphill. Now there’s a rule about high ground and orange juice.

mbm-0228.clue: The checks on this patch don’t line up.
mbm-0228.quote: I cut two old picnic shirts for our travel quilt. Where the checks meet, the red lines jump a little. My wife calls it the bump in the road where our picnic basket always slides.

mbm-0229.clue: My poles wear red ribbons in the lodge.
mbm-0229.quote: I picked up the wrong pair twice in one winter. Now I tie a bow round mine. A little girl asked if we were celebrating, and we took the lift together to celebrate fresh snow.

mbm-0230.clue: The chair has a notch for a sea shell.
mbm-0230.quote: I read in the sun with a shell wedged under the wobbly leg of my deckchair. I put it back on the sand when I leave. By morning the tide has chosen me a different one.

mbm-0231.clue: I look for the orange button.
mbm-0231.quote: Halfway up the indoor wall there’s a hold shaped just like the button on my old school coat. I can feel it before I see it. Once I find it I know exactly where my feet belong.

mbm-0232.clue: My towel has one square of deep blue.
mbm-0232.quote: At the pool I dive until the tiles turn the exact blue of that square. I brought my little cousin once and he insisted the towel was copying the pool, which is fair.

mbm-0233.clue: There’s a rubber stamp in my golf bag.
mbm-0233.quote: I caddied for my aunt when she made a hole in one. I carved a tiny flag stamp for the scorecard. Twenty years later I’m still carrying it in case it happens again.

mbm-0234.clue: I quilt the sky in one long thread.
mbm-0234.quote: My grandma taught me to rest the thread round my little finger. I stitched seven clouds without cutting it, then used the last inch for a lightning bolt. She felt that one with her thumb.

mbm-0235.clue: I run past an orchestra warming up.
mbm-0235.quote: The conservatory leaves a window open on summer mornings. I start the hill to a long violin note. By the time I come down they’re all playing and my feet have found the tempo.

mbm-0236.clue: Our relay baton is a loaf of bread.
mbm-0236.quote: We take turns jogging to the bakery on Saturday. The rule is you carry the loaf back with both ends intact. My father’s loaves always arrive suspiciously shorter than mine.

mbm-0237.clue: I had yarn left over after the teapot.
mbm-0237.quote: I crocheted a cozy for my mother’s teapot and a matching one for the sugar bowl. The sugar wears an absurd little hat. Nobody in our kitchen is allowed to call it a lid.

mbm-0238.clue: My favorite stop is down one flight of stairs.
mbm-0238.quote: On a sightseeing tour I heard music coming out of a basement. It was a clockmaker trying all his cuckoos at once. The guide lost three of us to those little wooden birds.

mbm-0239.clue: My lucky shoe squeaks on the last step.
mbm-0239.quote: I tried quieting the tongue with a strip of felt. Without that squeak I missed my spare. I took it out and the whole Tuesday league cheered when my shoe came back.

mbm-0240.clue: The crows know which ball is mine.
mbm-0240.quote: I put a blue dot on every golf ball so I can find it after a slice. A crow once rolled a blue glass marble out of the grass beside mine. We each took the one we’d brought.

mbm-0241.clue: I stamped a door into the corner.
mbm-0241.quote: I made a leather cover for my brother’s notebook. There’s a tiny door stamped inside the back flap. He makes me knock twice before I can read what he wrote.

mbm-0242.clue: The table leg has its own domino.
mbm-0242.quote: My cousins had to stop the game every time our table rocked. We tucked an old blank tile under the short leg. It’s the only tile in the house that wins every single round.
